From d1c44d9afa6f89aa0e10a191f30868eb12cd719f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>
Date: Tue, 27 Feb 2024 18:35:25 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] arm64: dts: rockchip: add missing interrupt-names for rk356x
 vdpu
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

The video-codec@fdea0400 was missing the interrupt-names property that is
part of the binding. Add it.

Fixes: 944be6fba401 ("arm64: dts: rockchip: Add VPU support for RK3568/RK3566")
Cc: Piotr Oniszczuk <piotr.oniszczuk@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Uwe Kleine-König <ukleinek@debian.org>
Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240227173526.710056-1-heiko@sntech.de

diff --git a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk356x.dtsi b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk356x.dtsi
index c19c0f1b3778..6a9bfb0550c0 100644
--- a/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk356x.dtsi
+++ b/arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk356x.dtsi
@@ -597,6 +597,7 @@ vpu: video-codec@fdea0400 {
 		compatible = "rockchip,rk3568-vpu";
 		reg = <0x0 0xfdea0000 0x0 0x800>;
 		interrupts = <GIC_SPI 139 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
+		interrupt-names = "vdpu";
 		clocks = <&cru ACLK_VPU>, <&cru HCLK_VPU>;
 		clock-names = "aclk", "hclk";
 		iommus = <&vdpu_mmu>;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/arm64/boot/dts/rockchip/rk356x.dtsi`**
   - Added the property `interrupt-names` with the value `"vdpu"` to the `vpu: video-codec@fdea0400` node.

### Relationships

- The modification addresses a missing property in the device tree source (DTS) file for the RK356x series, specifically for the video codec component. This change is part of a fix for a previous commit that added VPU support for RK3568/RK3566, ensuring that the interrupt names are correctly defined as per the binding specifications. The addition of the `interrupt-names` property enhances the functionality and compliance of the device tree with the expected hardware configuration.

Here is the commit message:
arm64: dts: rockchip: add missing interrupt-names for rk356x
 vdpu
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

The video-codec@fdea0400 was missing the interrupt-names property that is
part of the binding. Add it.

Fixes: 944be6fba401 ("arm64: dts: rockchip: Add VPU support for RK3568/RK3566")
Cc: Piotr Oniszczuk <piotr.oniszczuk@gmail.com>
Acked-by: Uwe Kleine-König <ukleinek@debian.org>
Signed-off-by: Heiko Stuebner <heiko@sntech.de>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240227173526.710056-1-heiko@sntech.de

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the absence of the `interrupt-names` property in the device tree source for the video codec, which is required as part of the binding specification. This omission can lead to improper handling of interrupts by the driver, potentially resulting in malfunctioning of the video processing unit (VPU).

Here is the patch:

+		interrupt-names = "vdpu";
 		clocks = <&cru ACLK_VPU>, <&cru HCLK_VPU>;
 		clock-names = "aclk", "hclk";

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```dts
interrupts = <GIC_SPI 139 IRQ_TYPE_LEVEL_HIGH>;
```
Reason:
The absence of the `interrupt-names` property in the device tree source means that the driver cannot correctly identify and handle the interrupts associated with the video codec. This can lead to improper functioning of the video processing unit (VPU) as the driver relies on these names to manage interrupts effectively.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```dts
interrupt-names = "vdpu";
```
Reason:
Adding the `interrupt-names` property with the value "vdpu" provides the necessary context for the driver to correctly associate the interrupt with the video codec. This ensures that the interrupts are handled properly, allowing the VPU to function as intended.
